Steve Hilton

Republican candidate for Governor, California · Open seat

Former senior adviser to UK Prime Minister David Cameron; former Fox News host; co-founder of a political crowdfunding platform

Steve Hilton is a British American Republican who served as senior adviser to UK Prime Minister David Cameron from 2010 to 2012, then moved to California and co-founded a Silicon Valley political crowdfunding platform. He hosted a weekly show on Fox News from 2017 to 2023. He advanced from the top-two primary to face Democrat Xavier Becerra in the November 3, 2026 general election for governor, the seat being vacated by term-limited Gov. Gavin Newsom.

Where Hilton stands

Taxes
Proposes eliminating state income tax on the first $150,000 of earnings, with a flat rate above that, and cutting the gas tax in half. Opposes Proposition 40, the one-time tax on billionaires' assets.
Business & Economy
Supports business deregulation. Proposes ending greenhouse gas mandates that he says raise utility costs, limiting lawsuits brought under labor and environmental laws, and eliminating the $800 business registration fee.
Housing
Proposes to 'bring back the starter home' by cutting fees and building rules for small single-family homes, plus a state loan program for first-time buyers. Would bar CEQA lawsuits used to stop construction.
Homelessness
Says street camping is illegal and that police should help clear all encampments. Proposes funding sober housing and recovery centers with addiction and mental health treatment, and overhauling state homelessness spending.
Climate & Energy
Proposes rolling back state climate mandates, ending rules that require utilities to buy solar and wind power, and allowing more natural gas production. Also proposes a volunteer tree-planting and forest restoration program.
Relationship with President Trump
Endorsed by President Trump. Says he expects a cooperative relationship with the president that would help California get more federal assistance.
Education
Supports school choice through education savings accounts and ending teacher tenure. Proposes banning smartphone use for children under 14 and pausing AI use in schools until summer 2027.
State spending
Says state spending has doubled in ten years. Proposes spending cuts, ending the high-speed rail project, reducing bureaucracy and acting against Medi-Cal fraud to offset his tax cuts.
